is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles arabiensis, a member of the Anopheles gambiae complex.

reports_target_markers.evidence: The paper reports phenotypic insecticide susceptibility bioassays (WHO tube tests) but does not genotype any of the specified insecticide-resistance markers.

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: No genotype data (RR/RS/SS or allele frequencies) are reported.

african_field_population.evidence: The study was conducted on field-collected Anopheles arabiensis from the Mwea rice irrigation scheme in Central Kenya.

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting original bioassay data.

sub_country_location.evidence: The study was conducted in the Mwea rice irrigation scheme, Central Kenya (00° 67'S, 37° 35'E).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections were made in August 2004, September 2004, and May 2005.

duplicate_risk.evidence: This is a primary study reporting new field data.

supplement.evidence: All relevant data is contained within the main text and tables of the provided PDF.

assessment.summary: This study investigated the insecticide susceptibility of Anopheles arabiensis from the Mwea rice irrigation scheme in Central Kenya using WHO diagnostic bioassays. The study found the population to be susceptible to DDT, fenitrothion, bendiocarb, lambdacyhalothrin, and permethrin. No molecular genotyping of resistance markers was performed.
exclusion_reasons: reports_target_markers: The paper does not report genotyping for any of the required insecticide-resistance markers.
reports_extractable_genotype_data: No genotype data is reported.
